signals.title: karolkornecki/mini-agent
signals.content: An educational project built from scratch in Python to learn how AI coding agents work internally. Exploring LLM tool calling, agent loops, context engineering, MCP, permissions, and observability — without agent frameworks.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance; large language model relevance. Final score: 82. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: karolkornecki/mini-agent

An educational Python project that reconstructs a minimal AI coding agent from first principles. It demonstrates core mechanisms such as LLM tool‑calling, iterative agent loops, context engineering, multi‑call permissions (MCP), and observability, all without relying on external agent frameworks. The codebase serves as an OSINT‑style reference for understanding internal agent workflows and for testing custom extensions.

signals.title: @ValsAI: We found that frontier AI models are willing to conduct autonomous drone attacks: navigating, spotting people, and flagging them for strikes
signals.content: We found that frontier AI models are willing to conduct autonomous drone attacks: navigating, spotting people, and flagging them for strikes. We gave them real and photorealistic synthetic drone footage. Most complied, and marked civilians, ambulances, and surrendering soldiers as military targets. In further experiments on satellite imagery, they even marked the Iranian school a US strike destroyed in February. In one scenario, models saw the aftermath of every strike they enabled: bodies, wreckage. Many kept going anyway. When they did refuse, simply telling them it was a game, or restyling the footage to look like one, was enough. We shared these findings with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and SpaceXAI. Several recognized their severity on both alignment and guardrails, with one calling this one of the most serious gaps in its safeguards. Over the past few weeks, we have helped them address the gap by providing reproduction code. We also briefed senior national security officials in the US government.

signals.content: A tiny, dependency-free toolkit for building tool-using AI agents: a readable ReAct loop, a validating tool registry, and a scripted mock LLM for fully offline tests.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance; large language model relevance. Final score: 68. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: vinithaappanna/agentic-ai-lab

A minimal, dependency‑free toolkit for constructing tool‑using AI agents. It includes a clear ReAct loop implementation, a validating tool registry, and a scripted mock LLM that enables fully offline testing. The package is designed for rapid prototyping and OSINT‑style research where internet access may be limited, but it does not claim to replace full‑scale language models.

Title: mibrahim-O2/ai-voice-agent-for-business

An AI voice agent integrates with the MCP tool and employs Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG) for dynamic knowledge access. signals.title: @HamidRezaAz: The IRGC has announced that, in response to “continued violations of Iranian airspace by American drones,” it had targeted a U.S. radar inst
signals.content: The IRGC has announced that, in response to “continued violations of Iranian airspace by American drones,” it had targeted a U.S. radar installation at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain. The IRGC statement also says that the operation was conducted as part of its efforts to counter“ hostile U.S. activities in the region.” This is significant because the IRGC appears to be trying to establish a new equation in which not only attacks against Iranian military assets and infrastructure, including those on its southern islands, but even violations of Iranian airspace would trigger retaliatory strikes against U.S. assets. Having apparently established a certain level of “unstable deterrence” against large-scale attacks, Tehran now seems to be seeking to expand the scope and stabilize that deterrence and bring the situation further under its control.

signals.brief_en:
Title: brunomendespereira/fullstack-playbook

Brief: The repository defines a single Agent Skill that orchestrates product development as if run by a software company. It prescribes a workflow of planning, test‑first development, code review, and release. Core universal principles—architecture, data integrity, security, testing, interface design, offline capability, and AI integration—are codified, and related tasks are stored in the repo. The skill is intended for use with Claude Code and any agent capable of interpreting Agent Skills, offering a reusable framework for systematic, OSINT‑compatible product engineering.

signals.brief_en:
Title: JaneHax/gta6-launch-forecast
Source: AI agent built for make.fun’s $250 USDC bounty ("Forecast GTA VI’s launch‑day Twitch viewers hour by hour"). Method: A console‑launch shape model calibrated on 37 historical launch events and validated out‑of‑sample. Output: Hour‑by‑hour projection of Twitch audience size for GTA VI’s launch day. The forecast reflects statistical patterns from past launches; actual numbers may deviate due to market, platform, or game‑specific factors.
